correctness.rationale: For a finite-dimensional realization, the first exponent \(m=dq\) yields the Zhou–Yang block form with an injective sector \(A\), cross term \(X\), and nilpotent sector \(B\) satisfying \(B^m=0\). Because \(A\) is finite-dimensional and injective, \(A\) is invertible; \(A^*X=0\) therefore gives \(X=0\). The injective sector has \(\mathcal{PQ}(A)=e\mathbb N\), and because \(B^k=0\) for \(k\ge m\), the tail of \(\mathcal{PQ}(T)\) equals the tail of \(\mathcal{PQ}(A)\), forcing \(e=d\). For \(q\ge2\), \((q-1)d\) lies in \(\mathcal{PQ}(A)\) but not \(\mathcal{PQ}(T)\), hence not \(\mathcal{PQ}(B)\); therefore \(B^{(q-1)d}\ne0\), so \(\dim B\ge(q-1)d+1\). If \(d\ge2\), \(\dim A\ge2\) because a one-dimensional operator has every positive exponent in its index set. The four claimed lower bounds match explicit constructions. No experimental enumeration is used as proof.

value.rationale: The focal theorem completely classifies which arithmetic tails can occur, making the least finite-dimensional realization a natural invariant rather than an arbitrary slice. The result gives a complete exact formula for every \(d,q\) and exposes a structural split between a periodic invertible sector and a nilpotent cutoff sector. It improves the source witness by \(d-1\) dimensions for every \(d,q\ge2\) and proves this improvement is optimal.
